clue.text: Proposed to give feed for development

indicators.note: development is growth or working up into a new form, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone suggests handing over animal feed to help something grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges FEED and FOR together; 'feed' looks like part of the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To have put something forward as available for someone to accept is to have proposed giving it.

clue.text: Having our nose put out of joint is hard to bear

indicators.note: a joint put out is dislocated, so the letters of these words are displaced into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken nose is a painful thing to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out of joint' rearranges the letters of OUR NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burdensome or oppressive is hard to bear.

clue.text: Squander food?

definitions.meaning: to squander is to waste, as one may waste time or money away
a piece of fried battered food, such as an apple or corn one

explanation.definitionFit: To waste money bit by bit is to squander it; a battered fried morsel is a food.

clue.text: Animal for which one horn will be enough

definitions.text: Animal for which one horn will be enough

parts.words: Animal for which one horn will be enough
parts.note: an animal often pictured with a single horn on its nose, though some species carry two

explanation.definitionFit: The Indian species of this large thick-skinned beast carries just one nasal horn.

clue.text: Party dress container found in good order

definitions.note: a person who belongs to a religious order, here a friar of St Dominic's order

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a mini is a very short dress or skirt
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: A party outfit is kept in a box that is neat and tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good order' sounds like tidiness, but it means a religious order of friars founded by St Dominic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a friar of the Order of Preachers, a religious order founded by St Dominic.

clue.text: It may support you if you retire in the country

definitions.text: It may support you if you retire in the country

parts.words: It may support you if you retire in the country
parts.note: retire means go to sleep, and in the country suggests sleeping under canvas, so this is something portable to lie on outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: A folding bed used when camping holds up a sleeper who turns in out in the countryside.

clue.text: Sailing-centre we found in Greek island

indicators.note: found in means one piece is placed inside another here

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is an island of the Greek Dodecanese
taken as written

explanation.surface: We discovered a place for sailing on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: COWES is a yachting town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast, home of an annual regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: This Isle of Wight town is famous for its yachting regatta, Cowes Week.

clue.text: Swallow seen on mother's feast day

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece seen on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
ma's is mother's in familiar form

explanation.surface: A swallow is spotted on Mother's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb but is the bird. MARTINMAS is the feast of St Martin, 11 November.
explanation.definitionFit: The feast of St Martin, 11 November, is a church festival and an old quarter day.

clue.text: Rich fabric with an outstanding design

definitions.text: Rich fabric with an outstanding design

parts.words: Rich fabric with an outstanding design
parts.note: outstanding here means literally standing out, a raised woven pattern on a luxurious cloth

explanation.definitionFit: This luxurious woven textile has a raised pattern that stands out from its surface.

clue.text: Glance shows a number in fault

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a defect is a fault or flaw
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A glance reveals a mistake in a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' is the verb meaning to bounce off at an angle, not a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow that glances off something is turned aside, as a missile skids away from armour.

clue.text: Select leaders? Have a wry smile about it

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece
wry means twisted or askew, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Faced with chosen leaders, one gives a crooked smile about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Select leaders?' with its question mark defines an outlook favouring a chosen few; 'wry' rearranges the smile and 'about' wraps it round the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: The belief that rule belongs to a chosen few is the outlook of an elite, a select band of leaders.

clue.text: A minor cricket side act defensively

parts.note: a ward is a minor placed under a guardian
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A young cricketer's team plays a defensive game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: To fend off or repel an attack is to act defensively.

clue.text: Expenditure for trips

explanation.definitionFit: Money paid out counts as costs, and journeys out are excursions.

clue.text: Cross one river, accompanied by goddess

indicators.note: accompanied by means the next piece goes alongside, following on

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.surface: One crosses a river with a goddess for company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cross is angry or furious.

clue.text: A gesture one doesn't care to make

definitions.text: A gesture one doesn't care to make

parts.words: A gesture one doesn't care to make
parts.note: it reads like a gesture one is unwilling to make, but it is the one made to show one doesn't care, lifting the shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: Raising the shoulders signals indifference, the gesture of not caring.

clue.text: It shouldn't happen to a sort of bird dog

indicators.note: sort means arrange, so these letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird dog should not suffer such a thing, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges OF, BIRD and DOG; the surface plays on the saying that something shouldn't happen to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation hoping something never occurs, a wish that heaven prevent it.

clue.text: One in the club has a whip-round for cheese

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the whip goes round the club man

parts.note: a cat is a whip, short for cat-o'-nine-tails
a member is one who belongs to a club

explanation.surface: A club member organises a collection to buy some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection of money; split, the whip is the cat-o'-nine-tails and 'round' wraps it around the club man.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft, creamy French cheese from Normandy.

clue.text: Male goes out, storm breaks, result confusion

indicators.note: goes out suggests things going awry, so these letters are put out of order
breaks means smashed up, so these letters are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A man goes outside, a storm erupts, and chaos follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes out' rearranges MALE to MAEL, and 'breaks' rearranges STORM to STROM.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool, and figuratively a scene of turmoil and chaos.

clue.text: Broken-down car banned from hoe-down

indicators.note: broken-down means smashed up, so these letters are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car is barred from a country dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken-down' rearranges CAR and BANNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe-down is a lively country dance party, as held in a barn.

clue.text: Supervise for a small charge

parts.note: a small charge reads like a low fee, but here it is a little child in one's care

explanation.definitionFit: To look after a young child while its parents are out is to supervise a small person in one's care.

clue.text: Book is in stock

definitions.meaning: to book is to arrange in advance, as a table or seat
a stock is a store kept back for later use

explanation.definitionFit: To book a seat is to secure it in advance; a stock is a store held back for future need.

clue.text: Police officer's half, hearted meal

indicators.note: half-hearted means half of the middle is lost, so one of the pair at the heart goes

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A policeman eats his evening meal without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of SUPPER is PP; 'half-hearted' removes one P. SUPER is short for superintendent.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal for a police superintendent, a senior officer.

clue.text: Golf score can make a good story

parts.note: par is the standard score for a golf hole
able means can, having the power to

explanation.surface: A round of golf can provide a fine tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb helping 'make', but it gives ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple tale told to teach a moral lesson, like those in the Gospels.

clue.text: Never rising to attempt critical stage of space flight

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Never getting up to try something.
explanation.walkthrough: NE'ER drops its apostrophe; 'rising' turns it to REEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The return of a spacecraft into the atmosphere is a dangerous phase of a mission.

clue.text: Graduates thus as a singer

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Graduates go on to perform as a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass voice, or a singer with the lowest male voice, especially in opera.

clue.text: Service men who have a job to do

definitions.text: Service men who have a job to do

parts.words: Service men who have a job to do
parts.note: armed services personnel assembled for one specific mission

explanation.definitionFit: A military unit formed for a particular operation, or any group set up for a specific purpose.

clue.text: Experience trouble in a test

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so these letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes through difficulty in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble in' rearranges A TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a taste of something, like a taste of hardship, is to experience it briefly.

clue.text: They burn sacks

explanation.definitionFit: Blazes burn; an employer who dismisses staff is said to give them the sack.

clue.text: Writers have a small room with key on board

indicators.note: to have something on board is to hold it, so the ship's letters contain the room and key

parts.note: on board is the crossword convention for a steamship, SS, which holds things aboard
a crib is a small room or hut
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Writers share a tiny cabin with a key on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the convention for steamship (SS), and 'have' makes that ship hold the small room and key.
explanation.definitionFit: Scribes were professional copyists and clerks who wrote documents by hand.

clue.text: Fashion arbiter of Welsh taste

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so these letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A trendsetter in fashion has Welsh taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the noun of style but is the verb rearranging ARBITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a Welsh savoury dish.

clue.text: Part of a lathe that could be altered

indicators.note: could be signals the letters can be turned into another word

explanation.surface: A machine component that might be modified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ALTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot pedal drives some lathes and sewing machines, a working component of the machine.

clue.text: Control may rest in the wrong position

indicators.note: letters put in the wrong position are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Command may lie in an unsuitable place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong position' rearranges MAY REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Command or dominance over something is having it under control.
